**Short answer: at least 30W. For fast charging, get a 70W USB-C charger.**

**Wattage by model** (from [Apple's adapter guide](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509) and the spec pages):
- **Minimum to charge:** 30W. Apple lists this for the current 13-inch M5 Air ([specs](https://images.apple.com/tm/macbook-air/specs/)).
- **What ships in the box:**
  - M5 (2026): 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max ([Apple M5 specs](https://support.apple.com/en-us/126320)).
  - M4 (2025), 8-core GPU: 30W adapter.
  - M4 (2025), 10-core GPU: 35W Dual USB-C Port adapter ([Apple M4 specs](https://support.apple.com/en-us/122209)).
- **Fast charging:** needs a 70W or higher USB PD source. Apple's recommended options for 2022-and-later Airs are 30W, 35W dual-port, 67W and 70W adapters.
- **Older Airs (2018 to 2021):** Apple recommends the 30W or the 40W Dynamic (60W Max) adapter.

Any USB-C charger that supports USB Power Delivery will work, even if its wattage is higher or lower than Apple's recommendation. Lower-wattage chargers will just charge more slowly. To check what a connected charger delivers, hold Option, click the Apple menu, choose System Information, then Power.

**A third-party option:** the [Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W (2-pack, 2× USB-C + USB-A)](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u) is listed at $49.99 on Baseus's US store (as of 2026-10-21). It's well above the 30W minimum, but it falls just short of the 70W fast-charge threshold. With two or more devices plugged in, the laptop port drops to 45W, which still charges a MacBook Air. This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission if you buy through it. The listing also says the price was verified on 2026-10-21, so check it at checkout.

If you tell me which year and size of Air you have, I can narrow this down. If you want true fast charging, look for a 70W USB-C adapter. Apple sells one, but I don't have a direct purchase link for it from these results.
